significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, among outcome-matched scientific inputs, higher internal “route separability” predicts greater within-route than across-route intervention transfer; this measurable coupling would constrain expectations about intervention generalization rather than merely show that route information exists. The claim establishes a representational phenomenon and evidence of functional route specificity, but not a full causal account of the established scientific mechanisms themselves; this matters because current protein-model interpretation exemplified by Vig et al.'s “BERTology Meets Biology” and InterPLM commonly relies on encoded-feature evidence whose connection to functional use is a key interpretive limitation. A negative result would reject the proposed Route-Separability Score as a general diagnostic and support route collapse in the tested models, although it would not rule out nonlinear or otherwise inaccessible mechanistic representations, so the two branches are determinate but asymmetrically informative. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve this score: deleting the specific “route-separability predicts…cross-route intervention generalization” relation leaves only the generic topic of scientific representations, whereas that predictive coupling is more constraining than the topic-median concept probe.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “Route-Separability Score” and the “outcome-with-multiple-routes benchmark,” with RSS proposed as a model-auditing predictor of route-specific intervention transfer. This can operate ex ante with respect to relying on or deploying interventions—models with poor RSS can be flagged before such use—although computing it requires known route labels and matched outcomes, so it is not a general-purpose screen for uncharacterized cases. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive RSS-to-transfer-specificity relation predicts what should recur, rather than supplying only a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction; however, the claim explicitly concedes that “Findings are outcome- and model-specific,” limiting transfer of absolute scores and route geometry. The asserted scope covers protein, molecular, and materials model classes, with likely uptake by scientific-model developers and auditors rather than outside-domain practitioners directly; the topic-substitution check therefore supports 7 only because the specific predictive audit handle and action window survive, not because scientific foundation models are broadly important.
